summary.oneLiner:
Standalone Q4 beat sharply on a weak base (PAT +368% YoY) while consolidated FY26 PAT was flat-to-down YoY on
fair-value marks on group investments, not the operating business; the real story is a multi-year diversification
push (MTF, PMS/AIF, Wealth, debt issuance via Share India Cred, uTrade algo platform, Tier-3 branch build-out) to
cut reliance on the ~49-52% profit contribution from proprietary trading, just as a new RBI circular (effective
1-Jul-2026) curbs bank funding support for prop-desk intraday trading.

financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > One-offs: consolidated FY26 PAT decline vs FY25 driven by fair-value adjustment on group-company investments, not operating weakness (mgmt claim). Standalone FY26 revenue figure appears internally inconsistent with the quarterly figure — treat with caution until clarified next quarter.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Margin guidance (reaffirmed, annual basis): EBITDA margin ~38% (+/-2%); PAT margin ~22% (+/-2%) — mgmt says Q4 dips (seen in both FY25 and FY26) are geopolitical-volatility driven, not structural, and should not recur every year.

MTF book target: ₹650 cr by FY27 (from ₹424cr FY26-end), contingent on "normal" market conditions — mgmt explicitly caveats this is not assured; low-single-digit downside deviation possible if sentiment sours.
PMS AUM target: ₹200 cr by FY27-end (from >₹100cr already raised in the PMS's first quarter).

Revenue-mix target: client-side turnover to reach ~60% (from >53% now) and client-side profitability to >50-55% (from ~49-52% consolidated / ~52% standalone) by FY26-end/FY27; 3-year aspirational goal is 70% client / 30% prop (vs current ~49-52% prop contribution to PAT).
AIF (CAT-3) launch: SEBI approval expected end of Q2 (FY27), operations targeted to start within FY27.
Wealth Management (3rd-party product distribution, under Charu Sehgal): operations to start Q3 (of FY27, per hiring timeline referenced on the call).

Branch build-out: 7 Tier-3 branches already live (Hyderabad, Indore, Bhopal, Varanasi, Agra, Raipur, Nagpur); 6 more targeted by FY-end; long-term goal of 30 ground branches over the next 2-3 years, each targeted at ₹10-15cr MTF/year.
Share India Cred (debt arranging): target ≥₹500 cr worth of NCD issuances by FY27 (6 issues closed so far since Q1 FY27 start).
Silverleaf HFT merger: NCLT approval pending, mgmt expects resolution "in a maximum [of a couple of] quarters" (imprecise wording on the call).

RBI prop-desk bank-guarantee/intraday-limit curb effective 1-Jul-2026: mgmt estimates ~20% reduction in overall deposits/limits used on the prop side but expects minimal bottom-line impact (per-trade margins should widen as ~₹40,000-50,000 cr of capital is estimated to exit the market industry-wide); existing bank guarantees continue until expiry — stated once as "up to 30th June" and separately as "by up to March 2027" (two different sounding dates given on the same call — verbatim, not reconciled).
order book & pipeline: Not applicable in the traditional order-book sense (brokerage/financial-services business). Pipeline proxies:
institutional empanelment up from 137 to 186 institutions (+35% YoY); uTrade algo-platform client base crossed
5,231 (vs >5,000 milestone flagged as "first time crossed"); MSCI (Metropolitan Stock Exchange) — in which
Share India holds a minority investment across two funding rounds — running ₹300-400 cr/day cash-market
volume and planning an IPO-listing segment, SME segment, and a derivatives segment in FY27 (subject to
regulatory approvals) — an optionality item for Share India's investment, not a "challenge."
segment / subsidiary detail: Standalone vs consolidated gap: consolidated Q4/FY26 profitability trails standalone due to fair-value marks
on investments held by group companies plus weaker market conditions at the group level.
Prop trading: ~70% of revenue but only ~49% (consolidated) / ~52% (standalone) of FY26 profitability;
client-side turnover crossed >53% for the first time (vs 47% prop) — mgmt frames this as a structural shift.
ADTO detail (Q4 FY26): options ~18% of quarterly ADTO; commodity ADTO reported as jumping sharply
YoY (mgmt cited "~14 billion" in the year-ago quarter rising to "~4,500-5,000" in Q4 FY26 — units/scale as
stated on the call, ambiguous, not independently reconciled); cash-market ADTO up from ~₹1,500 cr to ~₹2,000
cr Q4-on-Q4.
NBFC/MTF book: NIM of 17.64% for FY26, ~flat vs FY25; mgmt says NIM will likely trend down as the book
is grown more conservatively (secured lending, lower leverage vs FY23/FY24 levels).
uTrade: flagship algo-trading platform; multi-broker expansion (talks with Motilal Oswal, Dhan and others)
stalled by a new SEBI circular requiring third-party trading-tech vendors to set up separate infrastructure
per broker — cost-prohibitive at current scale; Share India (as the originating broker) continues to push
uTrade to its own retail base instead.
growth verticals / optionality: Wealth Management (3rd-party distribution + PMS, AIF pending), Debt Capital Markets (Share India Cred),
Tier-3 branch expansion (direct-to-customer model removing sub-broker/mediator margin), commodities
(prop + retail, benefiting from FY26 volatility in gold/silver/crude), international expansion (unspecified),
unlisted-securities segment, and the MSCI (Metropolitan Stock Exchange) investment optionality (cash market

spreads in under-served geographies (mgmt cites Hyderabad performing ahead of an earlier Calcutta branch).
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 margin compression (both FY25 and FY26) attributed to seasonal/geopolitical market volatility, not a
structural March-quarter pattern per mgmt; full-year guidance of ~38% EBITDA / ~22% PAT margin (+/-2%)
reaffirmed. MTF funding cost currently elevated because FY26-end borrowings will accrue interest for a full
year only in FY27; mgmt is working on cheaper NCD/third-party borrowing lines to compress spread over time.

2-3 years. AIF CAT-3 approval targeted end of Q2 (FY27). Wealth Management 3rd-party distribution ops targeted
Q3 (FY27). Silverleaf NCLT merger approval pending (timeline vague — "a maximum quarters' time").

converting intraday facilities into bank guarantees tied to the client book — a structural incentive for
